title: Constraints, benches & homework sheets · path still missing
theme: Agent tests/constraints, multi-model bench jumps, and AI homework all sell last-frame confidence. Push re-runnable tasks + score the path (agents and students).
briefing: Uncle Bob’s mega thread: don’t read agent code — surround with extreme tests/constraints. Sakana Fugu-Ultra v1.1: +7.9 bench points, ProgramBench / Terminal Bench, “beating Fable 5” without Fable in the pool. Cole: agents attaching annotated screenshots to PRs. Derek Guy: AI homework widens grade-chasers vs real learning. Growth angle: sit in these already-loud rooms with one process-vs-last-frame ask — profile visits from strangers, not quiet niche chats.

drafts.why: Root ~12.8k likes — largest room this pack; thesis fit is exact (tests as confidence layer). Nuance that green gauntlet still misses wrong delegated decisions.
drafts.body:
I get the posture. If you don't read the agent code, the only honest move is a hard gauntlet of constraints so the last frame isn't pure hope.

What I’m concerned as a builder: unit tests and coverage can all go green while the agent still took a decision you never meant to delegate. Same bug as a clean homework sheet with no thinking underneath.

Do your suites also score the path / intermediate choices, or only that the final container and metrics look right?
drafts.tip: Reply to root post on agent constraints; ~12.8k likes / high RT

drafts.why: Lab post ~2k likes / 200k views — discovery room of builders watching multi-model agents. Ask for fixed suite + re-run.
drafts.body:
Respect for shipping the v1.1 bump and putting ProgramBench / Terminal Bench numbers on the page.

I’m not totally getting the “beats Fable 5 without Fable in the pool” line as a final verdict though — is that on a frozen public task suite we can re-run next week, or the same chart set you already control?

Like when benches move 7–8 points in a patch, I personally always prefer a small fixed list + seeds the community can recheck over groundless excitement. Happy to be wrong if you point to the exact tasks.

drafts.body:
This is the right fear. Grades were always a last-frame score. AI just made it cheaper to buy a clean sheet without the thinking path.

I mean the people who only cared about the number will look even smarter on homework, and then causal reasoning on the real exam (or the real job) still collapses.

If schools only mark final submissions, they are training that bug. Score the process, not only the output — same problem we have with agents that pass tests and still decide wrong.

drafts.body:
This is useful. Screenshots are a tiny receipt of what the agent actually saw and did, not only “tests passed”.

I’d push one step further: attach the path (plan → what it changed → why) not just a pretty last frame of the UI. Green CI + open PR still lies when the decision was never yours.

Do you force that as a PR template or only when the agent remembers?

drafts.why: CEO amplify (~377 likes, 34k views) of same Fugu story — second room if lab reply is crowded; keep evidence ask short.
drafts.body:
Collective intelligence angle is interesting. Orchestrating a pool and still beating a named frontier on coding benches is a strong claim.

What I’m sceptical about as a builder: are those +7.9 points on a fixed, re-runnable suite (same tasks tomorrow), or a moving demo set?

Can you please clear things up with the exact bench versions / seeds so people can recheck without trusting the slide?
drafts.tip: Skip if already replied under SakanaAILabs — pick one room

drafts.why: Own thesis original for profile conversion after reply sprint; ties Uncle Bob + benches + homework into one path-vs-last-frame post.
drafts.body:
Green tests are not a verdict.

An agent can clear unit tests, coverage gates, even open a clean PR — and still take a decision you never meant to hand over. Same bug as a homework sheet that looks perfect with no thinking underneath.

Benches that jump 8 points in a patch have the same failure mode if you only ship last-frame charts. Score the path. Freeze the tasks. Re-run tomorrow.

Last-frame scores will keep lying — for models, agents, and students.

drafts.why: Short quotable for feed after hyper replies; converts visitors who saw Uncle Bob reply.
drafts.body:
Surrounding agents with extreme tests is necessary. It is not sufficient.

If you only mark the final container state, you are grading the homework sheet, not the thinking path.

I personally always prefer path checks + fixed re-runs over groundless excitement about a green bar.

drafts.why: Catch bench-watchers from Sakana room; evidence culture.
drafts.body:
When a multi-model agent jumps ~8 points on coding benches overnight, my first question is boring on purpose:

Same frozen tasks next week? Seeds public? Or a new demo set dressed as a verdict?

I’m not totally against the claim. I just want numbers the community can recheck.

drafts.why: Education lane follow-up; one soft process-assessment bridge.
drafts.body:
Secret AI on homework doesn’t create a new problem. It exposes the old one.

We already graded last frames. Now the last frame is cheap.

If you care about thinking, you have to score the process — in class and in agent evals. Final submissions alone will keep lying.

drafts.why: Mega author first post on open models; only if still climbing. Light thesis: open weights help community reverify, not just sovereignty slides.
drafts.body:
Open weights matter for a boring reason too: the community can re-run claims instead of treating closed leaderboard slides as truth.

World needs frontier closed and frontier open — agree. Just don’t let either one hide behind last-frame benches with no fixed suite.
